messages:
Maya (product): Quick sync — I've pushed a PRD draft for availability + graceful fallbacks. Need SLO targets and testable acceptance criteria before we lock the Q3 roadmap. Customers keep asking for predictable tail latency and an explicit degraded UX.
Priya (eng-runtime): Proposed baseline for short-text gen (<=256 tokens): p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 400ms. Availability SLO 99.9% monthly. Measure error budget as 1 - availability.
Dan (eng-sre): Sounds reasonable. We should be explicit about how we measure availability (5xxs, timeouts, or both?) and normalize across streaming vs non-streaming. Also we need error budget burn cadence (daily/weekly).
Maya (product): Good call. Let's define availability = successful 200/stream-complete within timeout. Edge cases for streaming later.
Liam (customer-success): Pilot customers asked if they can opt for 99.95+ SLA. They accept deterministic graceful degradation if we document it clearly.
Maya (product): Default SLO 99.9% for self-serve. 99.95+ as an enterprise SLA add-on with explicit penalties and runbooks. We need fallback modes listed in the PRD — what are we willing to do when SLOs threaten to breach?
Priya (eng-runtime): Ranked fallback options, from least to most disruptive:
1) Route to smaller/quantized model variant (fast, slight quality drop)
2) Prefer cached KV/prefix hits for repeated prefixes
3) Disable heavy features per-request (function-calls, tool hooks)
4) Return 202 with progress token for async completion
5) 503 hard reject as last resort
Dan (eng-sre): Add circuit-breakers. Also automatic rollback policy and operator dashboard with error-budget alerts and mitigation suggestions.
Zoe (eng-platform): Observability reqs: emit latency_ms histogram, p95, p99, fallback_type, fallback_count, error_rate, capacity_shard tags. Provide sample rates for histograms and retention policy (90d hot, 180d cold).
Alex (design): UX contract: when we fallback to a smaller model include header `X-Redwood-Fallback: model-small-v2` and response field `quality_score` (0-1). That way SDKs can surface a note or auto-retry.
Maya (product): Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Load test shows SLOs met under nominal capacity.
- Under simulated 2x traffic spike, fallback triggers within 5s and success rate >= 95%.
- Client-visible header present for all fallback cases.
- Rollout toggles per-customer via config flags.
- SLA docs updated with penalty math and enterprise tier language.
Priya (eng-runtime): Rollout config sketch: ```{ "policy": "fallback-first-fit", "variants": ["model-fast-q4","model-small-v2"], "circuit_breaker": { "p95_ms": 300, "window_s": 60 } }``` Feature-flagged rollout, with per-customer overrides.
Liam (customer-success): Add an opt-in for silent-fallback vs explicit-notify. Some customers want silent for latency; others demand an explicit degraded flag. I'll collect preferences.
Dan (eng-sre): Edge cases to call out in PRD:
- Streaming sessions: switching mid-stream can corrupt KV cache and produce incoherent completions.
- Function-calls: some depend on larger context vectors and should be exempt from fallback.
- Cross-region failover: tokenization/model-variant mismatches. Need an exemption matrix.
Maya (product): Agree — include an "exemptions" matrix per endpoint/feature and an acceptance test matrix per model family.
Zoe (eng-platform): Alert thresholds proposal:
- P99 > 400ms for 5m -> P1 page.
- Error rate > 0.5% for 10m -> P1.
- Fallback_count > baseline * 2 for 15m -> P2.
Dan (eng-sre): SLA math for the PRD: 99.9% monthly -> ~43.8 minutes downtime allowed. 99.95% -> ~21.9 minutes. Include examples showing how degraded-but-functional minutes count.
Maya (product): Owners & timeline: PRD owner: Maya. Eng lead: Priya. SRE owner: Dan. CS owner: Liam. Draft review by EOW (Fri). Implementation + QA in 2 sprints. Enterprise SLA docs by EOM.
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll add instrumentation hooks, the circuit-breaker, and a test harness that simulates model switch mid-stream. Will list exempt endpoints.
Dan (eng-sre): I'll add chaos/latency-injection tests to CI and the operator dashboard with suggested mitigations.
Liam (customer-success): I'll email pilot customers a short survey: silent vs explicit fallback + willingness to accept 99.95 with documented fallbacks.
Alex (design): I'll mock SDK flags, response header treatment, and a minimal UI banner for degraded responses.
Maya (product): Quick ask: drop any must-have edge cases here before EOD and I'll update the PRD and ping for review.
deploy-bot: Canary for feature/availability-fallback started for 3 hosts in us-west-2 :rocket:
Maya (product): SGTM :thumbsup:
Dan (eng-sre): TODO: add automated escalation playbook when fallback_count spikes and circuit-breaker trips.
Priya (eng-runtime): Noted — I will add a flow chart for fallback decisioning and a fallback telemetry schema.
Liam (customer-success): I'll draft a sample enterprise clause describing SLA exceptions and customer notification windows.
Maya (product): Thanks all — closing thread. I'll post PRD link once updated.
